headline: Giles Leads Georgia Past Arkansas in Defensive Grind
body: Georgia's passing game proved to be the difference Saturday as TJ Giles orchestrated a methodical offensive performance to lift the Bulldogs past Arkansas 24-17 in a contest that never quite reached full speed for either side. Giles completed 22 of 31 passes for 298 yards and three touchdowns, spreading the ball across multiple receivers and avoiding the mistakes that might have tilted a tight game the other way. Arkansas kept pace for most of the afternoon behind Jackson's steady hand and the intermediate accuracy that kept drives alive, but the Razorbacks never found the end zone when it mattered, settling for field goals in moments when touchdowns could have swung momentum.

The real battle unfolded in the trenches and secondary where Georgia's defense bent but didn't break when tested. Arkansas managed just 95 rushing yards against a Georgia front that made it difficult to establish any consistent ground rhythm, forcing Jackson into situations where he had to shoulder more of the load. Williams' 67-yard receiving day on only two receptions speaks to Georgia's willingness to take shots downfield, and those explosive plays created separation in what was otherwise a grinding affair where both teams managed the clock more than they overwhelmed it.

What made Georgia's victory complete was the discipline of turnover avoidance on both sides. In a game where field position and efficiency mattered as much as big plays, neither team surrendered possessions through fumbles or picks, meaning every scoring opportunity had to be earned through sustained drives. That zero-turnover purity favored the team with the better passing attack, and that was clearly Georgia. Arkansas had its chances but couldn't convert them into points when the margin was still razor-thin.
turningPoint: Williams' long reception in the second half gave Georgia a critical scoring position that ultimately produced a touchdown, pushing the Bulldogs ahead by more than a field goal and forcing Arkansas to play catchup with increasingly limited time.

unsungHero.name: Flores
unsungHero.why: Nine tackles and a sack meant Flores was in the backfield and involved on nearly every snap, yet Arkansas's offensive struggles meant his strong defensive showing couldn't be the story of the game.
